text:
ST. LOUIS, Mo. (First Alert 4) - A state representative is asking the governor to intervene in the ongoing budget battle between the city and the Board of Police Commissioners.

State Representative Steve Butz said he supported state control of St. Louis police, but says that the situation has escalated.

“What began as an effort to improve conditions for our police officers has become increasingly contentious,” Butz wrote in a statement.

Butz said the governor should step in, writing, “Given your well-earned reputation as a dealmaker, I believe your leadership is essential at this moment to restore functionality and cooperation within the board, rather than further isolating city leadership.”

The police department recently lost a court battle as it seeks to add millions of dollars more to its budget than what the city had allocated.

The police board provided a statement that read in part, “The Board’s focus remains unchanged: investing in public safety, supporting our officers and civilian employees, and ensuring the resources necessary to continue advancing safety across St. Louis.”

Tuesday, two higher courts dismissed the police’s appeals. Legal experts told First Alert 4 was a procedural error and failure on the part of the police board’s attorney, Chris Graville. But Graville denied that claim, telling us: “We did not make a procedural error. The Courts have now granted the much needed guidance to get clarify to move forward in the appeals process.”

Graville is a private attorney hired by the board. Recent invoices show he and his firm billing taxpayers more than $750,000 from July to February of this year.

Butz said the attorney general has the better expertise to end the budget battle.

The Board of Police Commissioners President Chris Saracino sent a statement to First Alert 4 Investigates that says, “As the Board works to remove politics from policing, we remain fully confident in Attorney Chris Graville and his team. Their guidance has been invaluable in supporting the SLMPD and helping navigate the complex transition to citizen-led governance.”

The police department said it still plans to appeal recent court decisions about the budget. Other lawsuits about the budget are also ongoing.
